verdicts.title: Long view on an own-half free kick hides the human's own taker and the ball (and near-side teammates in every long view on desktop)
verdicts.notes:
REPRODUCED in my own worktree at c59a889. Script /tmp/rt/camera-verify/out/s1-long.cjs (real page, ?renderer=3d&debug3d) sets a home restart, holds it in 'ready', lets the camera settle, then projects points through window.__derby3d's camera.
- Free kick at (40,60), 1280x800 (canvas 1041x697): data-camera=long, taker #8 = controlled. Ball projects to (-3,914) and the taker to (-21,922), both off-canvas. toWorld bottom-centre is y=50.2. The far touchline sits at py=140 (20% down), so the top fifth is stand. Only 4 of 10 outfield teammates are on screen: GK, all four defenders and #17 are off. Screenshot /tmp/rt/camera-verify/out/fk-40-60-1280.png shows only the edge of the orange aim wedge at the bottom-left, with no ball or taker.
- Free kick at (30,50): the ball is at py 694 of 697, on the bottom edge (fk-30-50-1280.png shows the taker cut off at the bottom-left).
- Goal kick at (5.5,39): the ball is visible, but bottom-centre is y=54.2. Teammates #6 at (23,64) and #10 at (48,63) are off-screen (gk-1280.png).
- 390x844 portrait: the ball is in frame but near the left edge (ndc x -0.82). The GK, 4 defenders and #14 are off (fk-40-60-390.png). The goal kick at 390 shows everyone (gk-390.png). So the near-side loss is mainly a desktop-aspect problem.
- Frequency, /tmp/rt/camera-verify/out/bun/fkspots.ts (20 CPU matches, MatchCamera at 1041x697 with the same restart focus): 144 free kicks, 100 in the taker's own half, 20 with the ball off-screen. All of those have y 51-66. That is about 0.5 per human per match.
Root cause: renderer3d.ts:108 returns y: HALF_H for every restart, so the frame never follows a near-side spot, and pushes the centre 0.32*width (23 m) upfield. camera3d.ts:197 sets tz = lv.z - width*0.12, which biases the frame toward the far stand. The long branch (camera3d.ts:189-206) never checks that the ball is inside the frame.
Fix (prototyped and verified): pass the restart spot through. Add ball: {x: sx(spot.x), z: sz(spot.y)} to the longView result (renderer3d.ts:87-108) and to the focus (renderer3d.ts:656). In the camera3d.ts long branch, after tz = lv.z - width*0.12, clamp tz so the ball's ground point is at least about 12% inside the bottom edge, and clamp tx to within about 0.26*width of the ball. Compute the near ground edge from vfov, elevation and aspect (camera height sin(e)*dist, bottom ray at e+vfov/2) rather than a constant. My prototype (/tmp/rt/camera-verify/out/bun/camfix.ts, a constant-coefficient version) gives 0/100 off-screen and 0 within 6% of an edge (fkspots-fix.ts). For (39,66) on desktop it puts the ball at ndc (-0.64,-0.65) and keeps the far touchline in shot (ndc y 0.96) and (72.5,34) in frame (fixcheck.ts). Add a tests/view.test.ts case that settles MatchCamera at 1041x697 and 358x448 for goal kicks and own-half free kicks at y=5..63, and asserts the spot and near-side full-backs project inside [-0.88,0.88].

verdicts.title: With a still mouse the player never reaches the pointer: the camera follow and the per-tick re-projection feed each other, and he can dribble out of play
verdicts.notes:
REPRODUCED in the real page and in a 60 Hz model.
Real page, /tmp/rt/camera-verify/out/s2-drift.cjs (1280x800, SwiftShader at 2-4 fps): carrier at (40,34), opponents frozen, mouse placed once and never moved.
- Aim 10 m ahead: at 6.2 s of sim he is at x=56.7 and still walking at 1.9 m/s. The world cursor slid from 49.9 to 58.5.
- Aim 9 m toward the near touchline (drift-ay9.log): he dribbles from y=34 to 68.3, and at 8.1 s phase='restart' and the ball is lost. The cursor slid from 43.5 to 74.0.
60 Hz model, /tmp/rt/camera-verify/out/bun/drift.ts (MatchCamera and the sim stepped together, renderer3d's focus, the client point re-projected every tick as input.ts:337-340 does, OneEuro as in take()), 6 s runs:
- Aims of 3/5/6/8/10/14 m: 9.9/17.7/21.6/30.0/38.0/44.6 m travelled, still moving.
- With the world cursor frozen: 2.4/4.4/5.4/7.4/9.4/13.4 m, stopping 0.6 m from the target.
- Aim 10 m: he passes the aimed grass by 1.6 m at 2 s and by 8.1 m at 3 s, so the overshoot shows within about 2 s, not only in long still-mouse runs.
- Aim (0,9): out of play at 5.6 s.
Refined root cause:
(a) input.ts:337-340 re-projects the stored client point every tick, so the target moves with any pan.
(b) camera3d.ts:168 drags the anchor at the edge of a ±5 m box (DEAD_X 0.09, camera3d.ts:63), and camera3d.ts:137 adds a lead of attack*2.5 + vx*0.5. After any run in a direction there is no slack left that way, so the camera pans 1:1 with the carrier at once.
(c) camera3d.ts:175 gives tz a gain of 0.8+0.35 = 1.15 on the near side. The cursor outruns the player toward the near touchline, so the gap grows and he speeds up until he leaves the pitch.
Variants (/tmp/rt/camera-verify/out/bun/camvar.ts + driftvar.ts):
- No lead: still 23-28 m.
- Dead zone 0.2/0.15: 15-18 m.
- Dead zone 0.25/0.2 with no lead: stops 0.6 m from the target.
The re-raycast follows research §2. But the README promises 'your player runs to the pointer' and 'a still pointer stays on the same grass', and the brief asked for no cursor drift while the camera moves; the existing test only covers weaving within ±1.5 m. It is not ball physics or pass assist, so it is in scope.
Fix: in input.ts take(), stop re-projecting while the client point is still. Latch the world cursor and re-project only on pointermove or a camera cut (snap, long view or replay end). The canvas has cursor: none (styles.css:615), so the ring staying on its grass reads correctly; optionally carry the pan offset into the next move so the ring does not jump. Or, on the camera side (camera3d.ts:137-179), skip the lead and use a dead zone of about 0.25 width when the human's own player carries the ball, and cap the near-side tz gain at 1. Regression test in tests/view.test.ts: still client point 10 m ahead, camera and sim at 60 Hz, the player must stop within 1 m of that grass, and none of the (0,±9) cases may go out of play.

verdicts.title: Phone landscape: the pitch is a 413x277 box in the middle of an 844x390 screen, and the HUD covers about 38% of it
verdicts.notes:
REPRODUCED. /tmp/rt/camera-verify/out/s3-layout.cjs at 844x390 with hasTouch, isMobile and dpr 2; matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)') is true.
Rects:
- #pitch x 215-629, y 20-297 (413x277): 49% of the width, 215 px empty on each side, and blank below y=326.
- .hud-tl 241x57 (58% of the canvas width).
- .hud-tr 102x118 (Menu, You vs AI, CAM, −/+).
- .hud-power at y 192-205 page (172-185 canvas), mid-right, because the coarse rule bottom:92px applies.
- Radar 100x65, Pass and Shoot 66 px each.
The bounding boxes sum to about 38% of the canvas. That overstates the painted area somewhat, but screenshot /tmp/rt/camera-verify/out/lay-landscape-touch.png clearly shows a desktop-size HUD over a small pitch.
Dynamic check, /tmp/rt/camera-verify/out/bun/dyn.ts (4 CPU matches, 75,798 live frames through MatchCamera at each canvas size, ball projected into the measured rects): landscape has the ball under the HUD 6.16% of frames (radar 5.45%, Pass 0.53%, power 0.14%), against 0.21% at desktop 1041x697 and 0.00% in portrait.
Cause: hud.css:2 `.match .pitch-wrap { width: min(100%, calc((100vh - 120px) * 1.531)) }` gives (390-120)*1.531 = 413 px; real phone browsers have less height, so the box is even smaller. The compact HUD sizes only apply under @media (max-width: 640px) (hud.css:95-112), which 844 px landscape misses. The 'end camera feet under radar' sub-claim was not checked.
Fix in src/client/hud.css: add @media (pointer: coarse) and (orientation: landscape) (or max-height: 500px) with .match .pitch-wrap { width: 100% } and #pitch.pitch-3d { aspect-ratio: auto; height: calc(100dvh - 16px) }; the 3D camera handles any aspect. Apply the compact HUD block under (max-width: 640px), (max-height: 500px). Hide .controls-hint there: hud.css:122 `.controls-hint.clamp` has higher specificity and re-shows the hint that styles.css:651 hides on coarse pointers, and hud.css:125-127 hides the 'All controls' expander, so the touch hint shows truncated and cannot be opened. Move the coarse power bar above the Shoot button instead of mid-right.

verdicts.title: Phone portrait: the power bar sits under the Shoot button (CSS cascade), Pass overlaps the radar, and 350 px under the pitch stay empty
verdicts.notes:
REPRODUCED, but the impact is smaller than claimed, so I downgraded it to minor.
Measured at 390x844 with touch and dpr 2 (/tmp/rt/camera-verify/out/s3-layout.cjs):
- Shoot x 298-364, y 388-454; .hud-power x 298-368, y 446-456. 8 of the bar's 10 px rows are under the Shoot circle.
- Pass x 222-288; radar x 159-231, y 412-459, so Pass covers the radar's right 9 px (the opponents' box on the radar).
- The canvas ends at y=464, the one-line hint at 494, and y 494-844 is empty.
- Crop /tmp/rt/camera-verify/out/portrait-crop-pad.png shows the red Shoot circle over the top of the power bar and Pass over the radar's right end (full frame: lay-portrait-touch.png).
Cause confirmed. hud.css:92-94 `@media (pointer: coarse) { .hud-power { bottom: 92px } }` is overridden by the later hud.css:107 `.hud-power { …; bottom: 8px; right: 6px }` in the max-width:640px block: same specificity, later wins. The computed bottom is 8 px (464-456).
Why minor:
- In dyn.ts (75,798 live frames, portrait 358x448), the ball is never under the pad, radar or power bar (0.00%).
- On touch the 3D aim wedge also shows the power, and while charging, the thumb on Shoot covers that corner anyway.
- The 844 px emulated height overstates the blank area: with real mobile browser chrome it is about 170-260 px.
It is a sloppy-looking overlap on every portrait phone match, but not broken play.
Fix in src/client/hud.css: add `@media (pointer: coarse) and (max-width: 640px) { .hud-power { bottom: 82px; right: 6px } .hud-radar { left: 8px; transform: none } }` after the 640px block, or move the coarse rule after it. Optionally use the free height in portrait: #pitch.pitch-3d aspect-ratio about 3/5 instead of 4/5 (hud.css:114), or put .touch-pad (styles.css:646) below the canvas.
